paper.title: Prior-free and prior-dependent regret bounds for Thompson Sampling

settings.name_in_paper: Bayesian multi-armed bandit with arbitrary prior
unmapped: Prior need not be of product form: reward processes may be dependent across arms; rewards i.i.d. conditionally on theta
settings.definition_quote: Let $\pi_0$ be a known distribution over some set $\Theta$, and let $\theta$ be a random variable distributed according to $\pi_0$. For $i \in [K]$, let $(X_{i,s})_{s \geq 1}$ be identically distributed random variables taking values in $[0,1]$ and which are independent conditionally on $\theta$. ... $\mathrm{BR}_n = \E \sum_{t=1}^n \left(\max_{i \in [K]} \mu_i(\theta) - \mu_{I_t}(\theta) \right)$

we consider here the two-armed bandit problem with sub-Gaussian reward distributions (that is they satisfy $\E e^{\lambda(X-\mu)} \le e^{\lambda^2/2}$ for all $\lambda \in \R$) and such that one reward distribution has mean $\mu^*$ and the other one has mean $\mu^* - \Delta$ where $\mu^*$ and $\Delta$ are known values.

the reward distributions are sub-Gaussian (they satisfy $\E e^{\lambda(X-\mu)} \le e^{\lambda^2/2}$ for all $\lambda \in \R$), one reward distribution has mean $\mu^*$, and all the other means are smaller than $\mu^* - \epsilon$ where $\mu^*$ and $\epsilon$ are known values.

conditions: holds for any prior distribution pi_0 over reward distributions in [0,1]

source.quote: For any prior distribution $\pi_0$ over reward distributions in $[0,1]$, Thompson Sampling satisfies $$\mathrm{BR}_n \leq 14 \sqrt{n K} .$$

results.notes: Thompson Sampling does not use n; MOSS-type index only appears in the analysis, so recorded as anytime. Computational cost depends on the posterior and is not discussed.

conditions: sub-Gaussian rewards with variance proxy 1 (E e^{lambda(X-mu)} <= e^{lambda^2/2})
